description: Figure 16b, titled “MMLU confidence vs. accuracy,” is a line plot illustrating the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for the MMLU dataset. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from 0.86 to 1.00 in approximately 0.01 increments. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in 0.2 increments. Three lines are plotted: “Final Accuracy” (solid blue line with square markers) remains consistently high, hovering near 1.0 across all confidence levels, with slight dips around 0.92 and 0.99. “Δ Accuracy” (dashed orange line with triangle markers) starts at approximately 0.3 at 0.86 confidence, declines steadily to near 0.0 around 0.95–0.97, then rises slightly to about 0.2 at 1.00. “Initial Accuracy” (dashed green line with circle markers) begins at approximately 0.65 at 0.86, increases gradually to about 0.95 at 0.98, then drops sharply to around 0.8 at 1.00. Error bars are present for all data points, indicating variability in measurements.
